- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.30) within 5 days of forecast, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of historical 30-day mean, adjust downward by 1–3% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.11) and forecast is above 75% of recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2%.  
- When sentiment is negative and forecast is high, apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.5% for each negative sentiment day in the prior 7 days.  
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment shifts sharply, wait 2–3 days before adjusting forecast.  
- If model consistently overestimates in bullish sentiment periods, apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day of sustained positive sentiment.
